title: FDA Modernization Act 3.0
official_title: To require the Secretary of Health and Human Services, acting through the Commissioner of Food and Drugs, to publish a final rule relating to nonclinical testing methods.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Earl L. "Buddy" Carter (R-GA-1) with 41 cosponsors and a cross-party original cosponsor group including Reps. Barragan (D-CA), Buchanan (R-FL), DeLauro (D-CT), Harshbarger (R-TN), and Carter (R-LA). The House-passed measure directs FDA to issue an interim final rule implementing changes Congress already enacted in section 3209(a) of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 — a narrow rulemaking-forcing mechanism that is the standard vehicle for accelerating overdue regulatory alignment and typically clears the Senate on the same bipartisan footing.

referencedSources.label: 21 U.S.C. 355 (Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act §505)

summary: Section 3209(a) of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (Public Law 117-328) amended Section 505(i) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355) to replace "preclinical tests (including tests on animals)" with "nonclinical tests" and added a statutory definition of "nonclinical test" — a test conducted in vitro, in silico, or in chemico, or a nonhuman in vivo test occurring before or during clinical trials — but FDA regulations in title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations still refer to "animal" tests. This bill requires the HHS Secretary, acting through the FDA Commissioner, to publish within 1 year an interim final rule replacing "animal" references in a listed set of 21 CFR sections with "nonclinical" and adding the statutory "nonclinical test" definition to CFR sections 312.3, 314.3, 315.2, and 601.31. The interim final rule takes effect immediately without requiring FDA to demonstrate good cause.
brief: Requires FDA to publish within 1 year an interim final rule that replaces "animal" references in listed drug and biologic regulations with "nonclinical" to conform them to the 2023 statutory change enabling in vitro, in silico, and in chemico testing methods.

top_lines.headline: Rulemaking Mandate
subs: FDA must publish an interim final rule within 1 year of enactment
Rule takes effect immediately without demonstrating good cause
Rule implements 2023 statutory changes to FFDCA Section 505(i)

top_lines.headline: Terminology Update in 21 CFR
subs: Replaces references to "animal" tests, data, studies, models, and research with "nonclinical"
Applies to 21 listed CFR sections covering IND, NDA, ANDA, radiopharmaceuticals, OTC, and biologic license applications
Plus "any other section necessary to ensure regulatory consistency"

top_lines.headline: Statutory Definition Ported to CFR
subs: Adds "nonclinical test" definition to 21 CFR 312.3, 314.3, 315.2, and 601.31
Definition from FFDCA Section 505(z): tests conducted in vitro, in silico, or in chemico, or a nonhuman in vivo test
Test may occur before or during the clinical trial phase

top_lines.headline: Technical Amendment
subs: Redesignates the second Section 505(z) — clinical trial diversity action plans, added by section 3601(a) of division FF of Public Law 117-328 — as subsection (aa)

sections.label: Section 2 — Regulations on Nonclinical Testing Methods

items.main: Requires FDA to publish an interim final rule within 1 year of enactment to conform 21 CFR references to "animal" tests, data, studies, models, and research to "nonclinical" terminology, implementing the changes to FFDCA Section 505(i) made by section 3209(a) of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 (Public Law 117-328; 136 Stat. 5821).
items.detail: The interim final rule must amend 21 listed CFR sections — 312.22(c); 312.23(a)(3)(iv), (a)(5)(ii), (a)(5)(iii), (a)(8), (a)(8)(i), (a)(8)(ii), (a)(10)(i), (a)(10)(ii); 312.33(b)(6); 312.82(a); 312.88; 314.50(d)(2), (d)(2)(iv), (d)(5)(i), (d)(5)(vi)(a), (d)(5)(vi)(b); 314.93(e)(2); 315.6(d); 330.10(a)(2); 601.35(d) — and any other section necessary to ensure regulatory consistency with the 2023 statutory change.

items.main: Requires FDA to add the statutory definition of "nonclinical test" from FFDCA Section 505(z) to 21 CFR 312.3, 314.3, 315.2, and 601.31, and provides that the interim final rule becomes immediately effective without requiring FDA to demonstrate good cause.
items.detail: The referenced statutory definition in 21 U.S.C. 355(z) defines a "nonclinical test" as "a test conducted in vitro, in silico, or in chemico, or a nonhuman in vivo test, that occurs before or during the clinical trial phase of the investigation of the safety and effectiveness of a drug." Notwithstanding 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B), the interim final rule takes effect immediately as an interim final rule without FDA having to make the traditional "good cause" showing.

items.main: Redesignates the second subsection (z) of Section 505 — the clinical trial diversity action plans provision added by section 3601(a) of division FF of Public Law 117-328 — as subsection (aa).
items.detail: The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 inadvertently created two subsection (z)s in FFDCA Section 505 — one defining "nonclinical test" and another requiring clinical trial diversity action plans. This bill's technical amendment redesignates the second (z) as (aa) so both provisions can be cited unambiguously.

underreported.section: Section 2(a)(3) — Immediate Effectiveness of Interim Final Rule
underreported.summary: The interim final rule becomes immediately effective without requiring FDA to demonstrate good cause, notwithstanding 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B).
underreported.why_unreported: The section is titled "Regulations on Nonclinical Testing Methods" but this paragraph waives the Administrative Procedure Act's "good cause" showing that normally accompanies bypassing notice-and-comment — a procedural choice not signaled by the section label.

underreported.summary: The rule must amend "any other section necessary to ensure regulatory consistency with the amendments to section 505(i) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 355(i)) made by section 3209(a) of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023".
underreported.why_unreported: The section lists 21 specific CFR sections but this catch-all clause gives FDA authority to amend additional unspecified sections — a scope-expansion mechanism embedded in an otherwise-precise list.

gaps: The bill sets a 1-year deadline for the interim final rule but does not require FDA to issue a subsequent final rule that would follow the ordinary notice-and-comment process.

The bill lists 21 CFR sections and a catch-all but does not address whether FDA's biologics-specific regulations at 21 CFR Part 600 (beyond 601.31 and 601.35(d)) or animal-drug regulations should be similarly updated.
The bill implements the 2023 statutory change but does not address the parallel FFDCA Section 351 (biologics licensing) which references similar preclinical/animal terminology.

The bill adds the "nonclinical test" definition to four CFR sections but does not require FDA to develop guidance for sponsors on which nonclinical methods (in vitro, in silico, in chemico, nonhuman in vivo) are appropriate for which drug categories.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Carter
featured_quotes.text: Many of our families would feel incomplete without the pets and animals that bring unconditional love into our lives. Yet every year, millions of animals, including dogs, man's best friend, are still subjected to testing in the development of new medicines. As policymakers, we have a responsibility to protect those who cannot protect themselves. That responsibility includes embracing scientific innovation that can reduce unnecessary animal suffering while continuing to deliver safe and effective treatments to patients.
